items.name: Inditex
clues: Arteixo, near A Coruña, in north-west Spain.
Its founder, Amancio Ortega, opened his first fashion shop in 1975 and became one of the richest people in Europe.
It is famous for getting new designs from the drawing board into its shops in just a few weeks.
Pull&Bear, Bershka, Stradivarius, Massimo Dutti and Oysho.
Its biggest brand is a fast-fashion chain with a four-letter name, starting with Z.
A short form of the Spanish words “Industria de Diseño Textil”.

items.name: Ferrero
clues: Alba, a small town in Piedmont, in northern Italy.
In 1946 a pastry maker started selling a cheap sweet spread made with hazelnuts, because chocolate was so expensive after the war.
Still owned by the family that founded it. In 2025 it bought a big American breakfast cereal company.
Hanuta, duplo, Raffaello and Tic Tac.
Nutella, Kinder Surprise and Kinder Bueno.
The family's surname, which is also the first word in the name of its gold-wrapped chocolates.

items.name: Alphabet
clues: Mountain View, California.
Created in 2015 as a new parent company for a famous internet business and all its side projects.
One of the most valuable companies in the world.
Waymo self-driving taxis, the AI lab DeepMind and the fitness tracker Fitbit.
YouTube, Android and, above all, the world's biggest search engine.
Another word for all the letters from A to Z. Its website is abc.xyz.

items.name: Mars
clues: McLean, Virginia, in the United States.
A family sweet business. In 1932 the founder's son started making his own chocolate bar in Slough, in England.
Still owned by the founding family, and one of the biggest pet-food companies in the world.
Whiskas, Pedigree and Royal Canin, and the chewing-gum company Wrigley.
M&M's, Twix, Bounty, and Snickers, which was named after one of the family's horses.
The family's surname, which is also the name of a planet.

items.name: Schwarz Gruppe
clues: Neckarsulm, in Baden-Württemberg.
It grew out of a wholesale business in Heilbronn, where the founder became a partner in 1930.
It is Europe's biggest retailer, but its owner almost never gives interviews.
A recycling company and a German cloud computing business.
Two supermarket chains: Kaufland, and a discounter that bought its name from a retired teacher for 1,000 marks.
The family name, which is German for “black”, plus the German word for “group”.

items.name: Unilever
clues: London.
Formed in 1929, when a Dutch margarine company joined forces with a British soap company.
Its products are sold in around 190 countries.
Knorr, Hellmann's mayonnaise and the toilet cleaner Domestos.
Dove soap, and Axe, the body spray that is called Lynx in Britain.
A mix of “Unie”, from the Dutch company's name, and “Lever”, from the British one.
